assumptions: #1298: an untimestamped v1 entry's run_id is `<suite>-<commit>-0-<sha256(canonical entry)[:12]>`. Two byte-for-byte identical untimestamped entries for one commit are treated as one run (the second is reported skipped), the same rule that already applied to two timestamped entries in the same second.

#1298: `Migrated N` counts writes. Ids already in the store are read through the optional AsyncHistoryStore.readAll (local NDJSON). The remote Supabase backend has no readAll and upserts, so a re-push there does write and is counted.
#1298: the migrated id shape is not the Python reference's (which used the wall clock); the timestamped shape is unchanged.

#1350: a test's flake identity is (test_file, test_name). Rows written before #1021 carry absolute or base-relative paths, so one test's pre-#1021 and post-#1021 history split into two rows; no path normalisation on read.
#1350: ci-ready's reason keeps the bare test name and adds ` (<file>)` only when two files in the window share that name, so single-file outputs are byte-identical.
#1350: the remote Supabase `canary_flake_summary` view is defined outside this repository and is not changed here; it still groups however it groups.
#1350 (F2 = a): ndjson-store.ts was paid down 299 -> 277 lines in a separate pure-refactor commit before the fix; no allowance or baseline file was edited.

#1352: guardian learns its own identity from its write: when GitHub reports the created or found sticky's author as someone other than the default identity, guardian records that login in a hidden `<!-- sticky-author: <login> -->` stamp right after the marker. A marker-led comment qualifies when its stamp names its real author. No new config surface, no extra API read or scope. The cost is one extra PATCH the first time a non-default identity creates a sticky on a PR.

#1352: #931 still holds. A human who pastes a stamped sticky is not adopted, because the paste is authored by the human, not by the login the stamp names. A user who deliberately forges a stamp naming themselves on their own comment can have that comment overwritten. That is self-inflicted and is accepted.
#1352: pr-comment.ts was paid down 299 -> 268 lines by moving the identity rules into the new guardian/sticky-identity.ts (re-exported, pure move) in a separate commit.
